clue.text: Famous seat in Derbyshire

definitions.meaning: a market town in that county, known for its crooked spire

explanation.walkthrough: Chatsworth is the stately 'seat' a solver thinks of first; the seat is a sofa, and the town is in Derbyshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep-buttoned leather sofa bears the name of a Derbyshire market town, so both readings of seat point to it.

clue.text: Mild sort of chap

definitions.meaning: a man's first name, borne by several popes

explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and pleasant, and it is also a boy's given name, so a kind of fellow.

clue.text: Nobleman, with honour, sometimes accommodates a sleeper

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman, decorated too, puts up an overnight guest.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeper is a small plain ring worn in a pierced ear to keep the hole open, not a person staying the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lower part of the ear is where a sleeper earring is worn, so it accommodates one at times.

clue.text: Photography in which petal semi-opens?

indicators.note: a flower that opens unfolds its parts into a new arrangement, so these letters are spread out afresh

explanation.surface: A question about filming a bud whose petals are half unfolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' rearranges PETAL SEMI; the surface fits, since this photography shows a flower opening in seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: This technique takes frames at intervals and plays them fast, so slow events like blooming appear speeded up.

clue.text: Engineers able to provide this second repair

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
fit means able, as in fit to work

explanation.surface: Army engineers who are capable can fix something a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a ship or building again is a further renovation, done after the original fitting out.

clue.text: As a joke, say, a lot of stuff for eating

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: in jest means as a joke

explanation.surface: Someone jokingly announces a great deal of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes IN JEST sound like INGEST; the A that follows completes it. The definition is a plural Latin word for food taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiologists use this Latin plural for material taken into the body as nourishment, everything swallowed.

clue.text: Oil applied to bats, wild in Leeds

indicators.note: wild suggests things running out of control, so these letters are thrown into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Cricket bats in Leeds get rubbed with oil with abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges IN LEEDS. Cricket bats are traditionally treated with this oil, pressed from flax seeds; Leeds is home to Yorkshire cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil pressed from flax seeds is rubbed into willow cricket bats to keep them supple.

clue.text: Brake for Victoria, for example, on coach

parts.note: Victoria is a London railway terminus
a wagon is a railway carriage or a horse-drawn vehicle, like a coach

explanation.surface: Someone stops a coach for a London terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: Brake is not the stopping device but short for shooting brake, an old British name for an estate car with a long rear load area.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting brake is a car with a rear cargo area and tailgate, the same body style as an estate car.

clue.text: Proposition from me to her?

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of these letters, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A romantic offer passing from one person to his beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges ME TO HER. The romantic proposal the surface suggests is really a proposition to be proved in mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic a statement to be proved from axioms is called a proposition.

clue.text: Stumps drawn on leaving pitch?

parts.note: reads like the close of play at cricket, but the stumps are cigarette stubs, drawn on as they are smoked and then dropped on the ground

explanation.surface: Cricketers pull up the stumps as they walk off the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'drawing stumps' ends a day's play; here the stumps are cigarette butts that have been drawn on (puffed) and dropped. Fag is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Fag is British slang for a cigarette, and the leftover stub after smoking is the remnant thrown away.

clue.text: Is one equally successful with ladders?

definitions.text: Is one equally successful with ladders?

parts.words: Is one equally successful with ladders?
parts.note: a board game pairs serpents with ladders, so the question asks whether a man skilled with serpents also does well with the other half of the game

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is as good with ladders as with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on the board game Snakes and Ladders: someone who handles the first half so well might be asked about the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who makes serpents rise from a basket with pipe music is skilled with the creatures that the board game pairs with ladders.

clue.text: Referee with work outside is in clover

indicators.note: outside says the work goes round the referee, enclosing him

parts.note: toil means hard work

explanation.surface: A referee with a job is living luxuriously, in clover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in clover' looks like the idiom for living well, but 'is in' is a link and clover is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This three-leaved plant is a kind of clover, and the name is also used for a three-lobed ornament.

clue.text: Piece laid down according to Mosaic Law?

definitions.text: Piece laid down according to Mosaic Law?

parts.words: Piece laid down according to Mosaic Law?
parts.note: Mosaic Law suggests the law of Moses, but read it as the rules for making a mosaic, where small square pieces are laid down

explanation.surface: A passage set down in the law given by Moses.
explanation.walkthrough: Mosaic Law is the law of Moses; the pun takes Mosaic as the decorative art, whose small tiles are each laid down in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of stone or glass set in a mosaic is the basic unit of that art.

clue.text: Dismissed soldiers for deviating from the usual

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British Army soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers sent away for not following normal practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for something eccentric or unconventional, beyond accepted bounds.

clue.text: It is held on the range in part of Texas

definitions.text: It is held on the range
definitions.meaning: the range is a kitchen stove, and what the cook grips on it is the grip of a frying vessel
the narrow northern strip of the state jutting out from the rest

explanation.definitionFit: A cook grips the long grip of a skillet on the stove, and the northern strip of Texas is named for its shape like one.

clue.text: But not 26's recording material!

parts.note: the arranger of music in 26 writes on staved manuscript, so this is the other sheet for jotting things down, a pun on musical notes

explanation.surface: A remark that something is not what the arranger uses for writing down his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer of scores records musical notes on staved manuscript; the answer is the ordinary sheets for writing letters, a pun on 'note'.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing sheets for letters and memos are what one records things on, though not musical notes for an arranger.

clue.text: How we looked as gales howled?

parts.note: gales are strong winds
to howl is to cry loudly, so to have wept

explanation.surface: Describing our dishevelled look during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Howled is not the noise of the wind but people crying; the definition describes a ruffled appearance after a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: After a storm one's hair is tousled and blown about, which is how one appears.

clue.text: He can retard a favourite, of course

definitions.text: He can retard a favourite, of course

parts.words: He can retard a favourite, of course
parts.note: of course seems to mean naturally, but it means on the racecourse, where a man may drug or interfere with the favourite to slow it

explanation.surface: A sweeping remark that a man may naturally hold back a favoured person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but means 'of the racecourse'; the man fixes a race by drugging the favourite. Nobble is British slang for tampering with a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobble is British slang for tampering with a racehorse to stop it winning, and the man who does it is the agent.

clue.text: Mean to deal in sea-food, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to deal in seafood is to sell fish

explanation.surface: A stingy person intends to go into the fish trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, 'intend to', but is the adjective, ungenerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is ungenerous and thinks only of himself is mean.

clue.text: Piece of rotten cheese or fish

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A choice between a bit of mouldy cheese and a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'or fish' takes in the link word: 'or' joins the hidden word to its definition, which is just 'fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater member of the carp family found in European ponds.

clue.text: Brown chap touching Circle Line?

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A suntanned man is near the Circle line of the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line; the definition reads geometrically as a line just touching a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a straight line meeting a circle at one point without crossing it is so named.

clue.text: More dapper French painter

definitions.meaning: smarter in dress, the comparative of a word for neat
Jean-Marc of that surname painted portraits at the court of Louis XV

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for smartly dressed, and the surname of the eighteenth-century French portraitist Jean-Marc.

clue.text: French tapestry lo! being woven

indicators.note: woven suggests threads interlaced, so these letters are worked together into a new order

explanation.surface: Behold, a French tapestry is being made on the loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being woven' rearranges LO BEING; the printed 'to!' is a misread of 'lo!', meaning look.
explanation.definitionFit: A Paris factory gave its name to the famous wall hangings it produced for French royalty.

clue.text: Wavering response from English poet

parts.note: someone undecided answers first one way then the other
the second half of an undecided reply, the affirmative after the negative

explanation.surface: An English poet gives an indecisive answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A dithering answer of 'no, yes' gives the surname of Alfred, the English poet who wrote 'The Highwayman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, author of the ballad 'The Highwayman', was an English poet of that surname.

clue.text: He speaks his words in play

definitions.text: He speaks his words in play

parts.words: He speaks his words in play
parts.note: sounds like an actor delivering lines in a drama, but describes a man who plays on words, making jokes from double meanings

explanation.surface: An actor delivering his lines in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: Play suggests a stage drama; read 'words in play' as wordplay, the stock in trade of a maker of puns.
explanation.definitionFit: A man fond of word jokes uses words playfully, exploiting double meanings.

clue.text: Cancel out fully in explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is entirely cancelled in a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' rearranges FULLY IN; the 'in' that looks like a link is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something void or of no effect is to cancel it.

clue.text: Accurate summary to a point

parts.note: a precis is a brief summary of a text
E for east is a compass point

explanation.surface: A summary that is right to the point is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and correct in every detail, which is what accurate means.

clue.text: Shorter actor can be one who scores

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A short actor might be a high scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges SHORTER ACTOR. 'scores' looks sporting but means writing musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranger scores music, writing out parts for each instrument in a full ensemble.
